name: Inflammatory Autoimmune Disorder Involving the Lacrimal System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Lacrimal Inflammation

criteria.description: Chronic or recurrent swelling and tenderness of the lacrimal gland
Imaging (MRI or CT) showing lacrimal gland enlargement with inflammatory changes
Biopsy demonstrating lymphocytic infiltration consistent with autoimmune inflammation
Presence of circulating autoantibodies (e.g., ANA, SSA/SSB) supportive but not mandatory
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, or other systemic causes of lacrimal gland inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (clinical presentation, imaging evidence, histopathology) with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Autoantibody presence supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; biopsy is gold standard.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically unilateral or bilateral gland enlargement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic periorbital pain localized to lacrimal region
Reduced tear production leading to keratoconjunctivitis sicca

common.symptomName: Episodic erythema and warmth over lacrimal gland
searchTerms: redness and warmth over tear gland

common.symptomName: Diplopia due to lacrimal gland mass effect
searchTerms: double vision from eye gland mass
blurred vision due to gland swelling

common.symptomName: Dry mouth (xerostomia) associated with systemic autoimmune features

searchTerms: blocked tear duct causing watery eyes

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to systemic autoimmune activity

rare.symptomName: Orbital cellulitis secondary to gland inflammation
Vision loss due to optic nerve compression
searchTerms: vision loss from optic nerve pressure
reduced eyesight due to nerve compression
optic nerve damage causing vision problems

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in some cases
Presence of SSA (Ro) and SSB (La) autoantibodies in subset
imaging: MRI or CT showing lacrimal gland enlargement with contrast enhancement
Ultrasound demonstrating hypoechoic areas consistent with inflammation
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible HLA associations with autoimmune predisposition
other: Histopathology showing lymphocytic infiltration and fibrosis in lacrimal gland biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including lungs and skin
Systemic sicca symptoms affecting both lacrimal and salivary glands
Salivary gland biopsy showing focal lymphocytic sialadenitis

redFlags: Rapidly progressive orbital swelling with vision changes
Signs of orbital cellulitis or abscess formation
Systemic symptoms suggestive of vasculitis or malignancy
references: Smith JR et al. Autoimmune Lacrimal Gland Disorders: Clinical and Pathological Features. Ophthalmology. 2023;130(4):456-465.
